title: Multi-step Variable Height Photolithography for Valved Multilayer Microfluidic Devices
protocol: Download a computer-assisted design (CAD) drafting program.
Define the 4" wafer area by drawing a 4" circle.
Place device borders using 300 µm polyline rectangles inside the 4" wafer outline.
Create different layers for each different height or photoresist needed for the final design.
Design features of a particular desired height on the corresponding layer.
Make device borders, global text, and the wafer outline on their own layer for global alignment.
Use closed zero-width polylines to design device features within device borders.
Clean and dehydrate a 4" test-grade silicon wafer.
Rinse the wafer well with methanol.
Blow dry with N2 or compressed air.
Bake on an aluminum hotplate at 95 °C for 10 min.
Place the cleaned wafer on a spin coater.
Turn on the vacuum to affix it to the spin chuck.
Blow away dust with N2 or compressed air.
Apply 1-2 ml of SU-8 2005 negative photoresist in center of wafer.
Spin as follows: spread at 500 rpm for 10 sec, acceleration 133 rpm/s; cast at 3,000 rpm for 40 sec, acceleration 266 rpm/s.

Remove the wafer and soft bake by switching between two hotplates set at 65 °C and 95 °C according to a specific program: first on 65 °C for 2 min, then switch to 95 °C for 3 min, finally back to 65 °C for 2 min.
Allow wafer to cool to room temperature.
Place wafer in the chuck of a UV mask aligner and expose without a mask ('flood exposure') for 20 seconds at ~6.2 mW/cm² lamp intensity.
If available, select hard contact mode to achieve a 300 µm wafer: mask separation.
Remove wafer from aligner.
Post-exposure bake by switching the wafer between two hotplates set at 65 °C and 95 °C as follows: 65 °C for 2 minutes, 95 °C for 4 minutes, then 65 °C for another 2 minutes.
Use online AZ50 XT valve predictor resource to plan spin speeds for desired valve dimensions and heights.
Place the wafer on a spin coater.
Turn on vacuum to affix it to the spin chuck.
Blow away dust with N₂ or compressed air.
Apply 2-3 mL of AZ50 XT positive photoresist to center of the wafer.
Spin as follows: spread at 200 rpm for 10 seconds, cast at 1,200 rpm for 40 seconds, snap spin at 3,400 rpm for 1 second.
Lay down the wafer carefully in a 5" Petri dish and let relax for 20 minutes.
Soft bake the wafer on a hotplate: 65 °C to 112 °C for 22 minutes with a ramping speed of 450 °C/h.
Remove the wafer from the hotplate.
Let rest overnight at room temperature in a Petri dish for ambient rehydration.
Tape Flow Round transparency mask to 5" glass plate print-side down and load into mask positioner of the UV mask aligner.
Expose the wafer to 930 mJ of UV in 6 cycles (25 sec each at ~6.2 mW/cm² lamp intensity, with 30 s wait time between exposures).
Develop the wafer immediately by immersing it in a stirred bath of AZ500k 1:3 Developer for 3-5 min or until the bath turns purple and features emerge.
Remove the wafer from the developer and rinse well with DI water.
Assess pre-reflow height using a profilometer (stylus force of 10.5 mg, length 1,000 µm, speed 200 µm/s, regime down-up).
Reflow hard bake the wafer to melt and round valve features at 65 °C - 190 °C for 15 hr with a ramping speed of 10 °C/hr.
Let the wafer cool to room temperature.
Assess post-reflow height using a profilometer (stylus force of 10.5 mg).
Proceed to variable height fabrication with the developed wafer using Flow Low, Flow High, and Herringbone Mixer transparencies of the Bead Synthesizer design.
Use manufacture data sheets to determine exposure energy, spin speeds, and bake time parameters within ± 5% tolerance.
Place the cleaned wafer on the spin coater and turn on vacuum to affix it to the spin chuck.
Blow away dust with N2 or compressed air.
Apply 1-2 ml of SU-8 2050 negative photoresist to the center of the wafer.
Spin the wafer at 500 rpm for 10 seconds, accelerating at 133 rpm/sec.
Continue spinning at 3,000 rpm for 40 seconds, accelerating at 266 rpm/sec.
Spin photoresist over developed valve features.
Carefully place the spun wafer in a 5" Petri dish and let it relax on a flat surface for 20 minutes or until streaking patterns fade.
Remove the wafer from the Petri dish.
Soft bake by placing the wafer on two hotplates set at 65 °C and 95 °C: 65 °C for 2 min, 95 °C for 8 min, then 65 °C for another 2 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature.
Tape the Flow Low transparency mask to a quartz 5" glass plate print-side down and load into the UV mask aligner.
Place the wafer in UV mask aligner chuck.
Align new Flow Low layer features to Flow Round valve layer features using microscope eyepiece or camera.
Align horizontal, vertical, and tilt axes of device borders to the device border features on mask.
Align cross-hair features between layers.
Confirm that valve features intersect Flow Low features where applicable.
Expose wafer to 170 mJ UV deposition (28 sec at ~6.2 mW/cm²).
Remove wafer from aligner and post-exposure bake by switching between two hotplates set at 65 °C and 95 °C: 65 °C for 2 min, 95 °C for 9 min, then 65 °C for 2 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to RT without developing.
Repeat steps using SU-8 2025 and the Flow High layer mask with spin coat settings of spread: 500 rpm, 10 sec, 133 rpm/s acceleration; cast: 3,500 rpm, 40 sec, 266 rpm/sec acceleration.
Expose wafer to 198 mJ UV deposition (32 s at ~6.2 mW/cm²).
Allow the wafer to cool to RT without developing.
Proceed to fabrication of Chaotic Mixer Herringbone layer.
Clean the wafer.
Dehydrate the wafer.
Fabricate a 5 µm adhesion layer on a new 4" silicon wafer.
Apply 1-2 ml of SU-8 2025 negative photoresist in the center of the wafer.
Spin coat the wafer at spread: 500 rpm, 10 sec, 133 rpm/s acceleration; cast: 3,500 rpm, 40 sec, 266 rpm/sec acceleration.
Remove the wafer from the spin coater.
Soft bake the wafer by switching between two hotplates set at 65 °C and 95 °C as follows: 65 °C: 2 min, 95 °C: 5 min, 65 °C: 2 min.
Align the control transparency mask to a 5" glass plate.
Load the aligned mask and glass plate into the UV mask aligner.
Place the wafer in the chuck of the UV mask aligner.
Expose the wafer to 155 mJ UV deposition (25 sec at ~6.2 mW/cm² lamp intensity).
Remove the wafer from the UV mask aligner.
Post-exposure bake by switching between two hotplates set at 65 °C and 95 °C: 65 °C for 2 min, then 95 °C for 6 min, then 65 °C for another 2 min.
Immerse the wafer in a stirred bath of 25 ml SU-8 Developer in a 6" glass dish for 1 minute or until features emerge.
Check the developed features using a stereoscope.
Hard bake the wafer to stabilize photoresist features: ramp from 65 °C to 165 °C at a speed of 120 °C/hr, hold at 165 °C for 2 hr 30 min.
Place the completed wafers in a wafer rack within a bell-jar vacuum desiccator inside a fume hood free of water or water-soluble reagents.
Apply 1 drop of trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane (PFOTS) to a glass slide and place it in the desiccator.
Close the desiccator lid and apply vacuum for 1 minute.
Turn off the vacuum without re-pressurizing or evacuating the bell jar.
Let the mixture sit for 10 minutes while aerosolized PFOTS coats the wafer surface.
Open the bell jar lid and remove the treated wafer using tweezers.
Place the silane-coated wafer into a Petri dish for PDMS replica molding.
Fabricate multilayer microfluidic devices in a "push up" geometry on glass according to existing open-access protocols.
Ensure all valves are aligned properly to control lines and all inlets (on both the flow and control layers) are punched fully before proceeding.
Connect tubing loaded with water to a flow control system.
Connect metal pins to tubing and connect to device ports at control line inlets.
Pressurize device control lines by setting the flow control system of choice to 25 psi for each line.
Ensure that valves close and re-open by inspection under the microscope.
Prepare custom microfluidic pressure vessels for reagent and oil loading.
Using a push-pin, punch two holes in the top of a cryogenic vial tube.
Insert capillary PEEK tubing into one hole.
Insert a metal pin connected to the tubing into the second hole.
Seal tubing in place with epoxy.
Let dry for 1 hr.
While waiting, suspend 3.9 mg of LAP photoinitiator into 100 µl of DI water in a microcentrifuge tube to prepare photoinitiator solution.
Protect photoinitiator solution from light.
Add 132 µl DI water, 172 µL PEG diacrylate, 12 µl LAP solution, and 85 µL HEPES buffer to a microcentrifuge tube to make hydrogel droplet solution.
Transfer the hydrogel droplet solution to the completed cryogenic tube vessel.
Connect the tubing of the cryogenic tube vessel to a controllable pressure source.
Connect the PEEK tubing to the device reagent inlet.
Prepare 10 mL of light mineral oil with 2% v/v nonionic surfactant and 0.05% EM90 for oil droplet emulsion.
Filter the prepared oil mixture using a 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Load 1 ml of filtered oil mixture into a second cryogenic tube vessel.
Insert PEEK tubing at the device outlet for collection of droplets.
Pressurize oil, water, or PEG mixture inlets (4 psi operational pressure) to remove air bubbles from the device.
Turn on all valves.
Sequentially turn off each valve in a fluid pathway after 1 min or until air bubbles have permeated through the PDMS device.
Depressurize Inlet 1, Mix 1 out, and Mix Waste once air bubbles are gone when de-bubbling herringbone mixers.
Repressurize the device after debubbling.
Set oil pressure to 10 psi by depressurizing Ro1 oil valve.
Set PEG mixture pressure to 9 psi and adjust upstream valves (Inlet 1, Drops 1) as necessary to produce droplets of the desired size.
Position a 5 mm spot from a UV light source over the polymerization region of the device.
Apply 100 mW/cm2 UV (365 nm) from the UV source.
Pressurize bead sieve valve to watch polymerized beads collect and ensure that droplets have hardened into beads.
Adjust LLG as necessary to achieve full polymerization.
Depressurize bead sieve valve and collect beads into tube through outlet PEEK tubing.
